title: 14-point type legibility preference for older adults
statement:
For older adults reading online text, 14-point type was rated more legible and was preferred over 12-point type, so senior-facing interfaces should start around 14pt and consider larger sizes when density is less important.

Options:
- Senior baseline: 14pt (fits: accessible, balanced)
- Comfortable: 16pt (fits: comfortable, friendly)
- Reading mode: 18pt (fits: access-first, editorial)
- Large print: 20pt (fits: minimal, access-first)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web, web apps, content sites. Audience: seniors, general.

source.title: The effects of font type and size on the legibility and reading time of online text by older adults
source.authors: Michael L. Bernard; Chia Hui Liao; Melissa M. Mills
source.venue: CHI '01 Extended Abstracts on Human Factors in Computing Systems
